title: Zero-trust offline upgrade contract for private/VPC deployments — clarified requirements and acceptance
creator: Anika Patel
description: Clarify and codify the upgrade and networking acceptance criteria for Private/VPC customers who require 'zero-trust' or fully air-gapped upgrade workflows. This PRD captures edge constraints (no direct egress, signed artifacts only, KMS rotation caveats), operational runbooks, test harnesses, and required telemetry fallback behaviors so that the platform team and operators have a deterministic contract for upgrades and emergency patches.
background: Several enterprise customers requested a formal contract for upgrades when their clusters are configured with zero or highly restricted egress. Prior artifacts focus on staged mirrors, proxies, and operator-based bootstraps; customers with zero-trust policies require: deterministic artifact provenance, operatorless applies, physical-media fallback paths, clearly scoped quiesce windows, and explicit telemetry privacy modes. This ticket standardizes acceptance criteria so engineering and solutions can sign off before release.
scope_inclusions: Signed artifact bundles (OCI tar + detached signature) and deterministic checksum validation at the node level
Offline upgrade command that consumes a pre-signed bundle delivered via customer mirror, SFTP, or physical media
Operator automation to validate signature chain and rollback on checksum mismatch
KMS/HSM key rotation handshake that can operate with an offline key wrapper (customer-provided offline wrapping key)
Explicit quiesce APIs for model-serving traffic and KV cache snapshot prior to upgrade
Minimal telemetry: health-only pings persisted locally and exported post-upgrade when allowed
scope_exclusions: Any workflow that requires direct contact to public cloud artifact registries during the upgrade
Automatic OS-level package downloads (apt/yum) as part of the upgrade bundle install
Unverified third-party connector installs that change network stack during the upgrade
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: Upgrade can be executed in a closed network (no outbound internet). All required artifacts are consumed from a customer-controlled mirror or physical media.
AC-2: Every upgrade bundle is cryptographically signed. Node-level verifier rejects unsigned or tampered bundles with non-ambiguous error codes and suggested remediation steps.
AC-3: Operatorless apply mode: cluster nodes can transition through the upgrade without requiring an external operator component to reach out-of-band resources.
AC-4: KMS rotation path validates new wrapped key offline; rotation must not require active HSM connectivity to Redwood control plane during critical-window operations.

AC-5: Upgrade includes a deterministic rollback plan: if >3% of serving instances fail health checks within the post-upgrade grace window (configurable), automatic rollback triggers using previous validated bundle.

AC-6: Telemetry sent during upgrade is limited to a single, customer-configurable payload that contains status (started/succeeded/failed) and non-sensitive health metrics; sensitive logs are stored locally until an explicit post-upgrade export is triggered.
AC-7: Upgrade test harness must include a simulated network partition test where mirrors are reachable but external internet is not; result must pass with exit code 0 for acceptance.
AC-8: Operator documentation and runbook (playbook) exist and include step-by-step instructions for physical-media based re-image and checksum reconciliation.
AC-9: All acceptance tests are reproducible via CI job private-upgrade/offline-canary that runs against a local VM cluster image and artifacts signed with test keys.
AC-10: Time-to-restore SLA: for critical hotfix path using physical media, operator can recover serving within the documented maintenance window (default 4 hours) and this is verified in a rehearsal.
AC-11: RBAC acceptance: only identities with the explicit upgrade role (scoped to cluster) can initiate an offline upgrade; audit events record the invoking principal and bundle digest.
AC-12: No secrets (unwrapped keys, private certs) are transmitted off-cluster during any acceptance test; tests must assert that no outbound sockets open to hosts outside the allowed mirror list.
migration_plan: Provide a two-track migration: (1) guided migration for customers using Redwood operator with restricted egress — we provide a signed bundle builder and mirror bootstrap scripts; (2) operatorless path for customers who require fully air-gapped upgrades — deliverable includes an image builder, signature tooling, and a physical media checklist. Both tracks include a mandatory rehearsal with the customer and one dry-run where telemetry is captured but not exported.
test_plan: TP-1: Local VM cluster test — use private-upgrade CI: create pre-upgrade snapshot, deliver signed bundle to local mirror, execute offline upgrade job, validate serving health and KV cache integrity.
TP-2: Partition simulation — block internet at firewall level but allow mirror CIDR; verify bundle consumption and service continuity across upgrade.
TP-3: Signature tamper test — corrupt one byte of signature; verify node-level reject and audit log entry contains bundle digest and rejection reason.
TP-4: Physical media rehearse — operator imports bundle from USB image, runs upgrade, verifies checksums and rollback path in a staging cluster.

TP-5: KMS offline rotation validation — wrap a test data key with the customer-provided offline key, perform rotation simulation without HSM contact, and validate encrypted token acceptance post-rotation.
rollout_strategy: Staged concentric rollout for Dedicated and Private clusters: (1) Small operator-run rehearsal on a staging cluster; (2) Customer joint rehearsal on a single production-like site (low-traffic); (3) Gradual site-by-site rollouts where the operator releases signed bundles and instructs on mirror sync procedures. Rollouts must be accompanied by a blue/green serving toggle and KV cache warmup to preserve latency SLOs.

open_questions: Q1: For customers with HSM-only key policies, can we rely on a pre-shared wrapped key model or is physical HSM shipment required? (Decision impacts KMS rotation acceptance)
Q2: Do we need to provide an offline artifact-hosting appliance image for customers who do not want to run their own mirror?
Q3: Should the default maintenance window be 4 hours or configurable per-customer contract?
Q4: What logging level is acceptable to include in the single telemetry payload during upgrades to satisfy both support and privacy constraints?
decisions_log: 2026-03-11: Decided to require detached signatures (RFC 7517 compatible) for bundles rather than embedded PKCS7; reason: easier verification on resource-constrained nodes.
2026-03-12: Chose 'operatorless apply' as a required capability for zero-trust contracts; fallback via operator mode remains supported but not mandatory for acceptance.
2026-03-14: Set default rollback threshold to 3% failing health checks; team can make this configurable per contract.
